name: kinu
description: Kinu gives AI agents a durable computer of their own. It adapts and improves with use, runs locally or fully in the cloud, and solves hard tasks by exploring multiple approaches and letting executable checks choose the winner.
//workspaces: third_party/mossaic/sdk is @mossaic/sdk, vendored SOURCE at one upstream commit because upstream publishes no npm package. It is named exactly, not by a `third_party/*` glob: the closure it builds from (shared/, worker/core/) sits beside it at the upstream-relative paths its own imports and its `@shared` alias require, and those are vendored bytes, not packages.

//dependencies:@ai-sdk: The AI SDK v6 packages are pinned EXACTLY in every workspace that declares one (the root declares only what its own scripts and fixtures import), because upstream pins them to each other exactly: `ai@6.0.214` requires `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@4.0.33` and `@ai-sdk/gateway@3.0.139` by exact version, and each provider does the same. A caret on any one of them therefore does not age it independently — it floats that package ahead of the rest and bun answers with a SECOND copy of the SDK nested under whichever parent disagreed, which is how `@ai-sdk/provider` came to be installed twice while both manifests named one version. So the cohort moves as one edit. This one is GHSA-866g-f22w-33x8 (CVE-2026-8769, uncontrolled resource consumption in provider-utils' response handlers), whose first patched release on the v6 line is provider-utils 4.0.33; these are the earliest same-major releases that pin it. Later v6 releases exist and are also patched, but from `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@2.0.70` the provider throws its own "Response stream ended without a finish reason" before a finish-step lands, which pre-empts the dead-stream detector in packages/core/src/chat.ts and the two contracts unit-chat-stream-integrity.test.ts holds over it. Moving past that boundary is a stream-integrity decision, not a dependency refresh. Float the cohort once upstream ranges its own packages instead of pinning them to each other.
//dependencies:effect: `effect` is pinned EXACTLY to 4.0.0-rc.117 wherever a workspace declares it (core; cf-backend for its workerd probe; the root for the red half of `gate:effect-diagnostics`), by owner decision on 2026-09-23: the error model runs on Effect 4's typed failure channel, and 4.0.0 is a release candidate (npm `rc` tag; `latest` is 3.22.2). A caret on an RC floats to the next RC, and RCs move API, so a bump is one deliberate edit in every manifest at once. `@effect/tsgo` is pinned exactly for the same reason: 0.45.0 lists TypeScript 7.0.2, and `gate:effect-diagnostics` fails when its planted floating effect stops being reported, so a bump cannot switch the check off in silence. Float both once Effect 4.0.0 is a stable release.
//devDependencies:bun: Bun 1.4.3 carries both oven-sh/bun#44279 (retired-realm crashes, which the canary pin was for) and #44581 (13a98b0dbd), whose absence left a synchronous spawn spinning over a zombie child: the production deploy contract row went silent in 12 of 48 runs on canary 9bd19c98e and 0 of 96 on 1.4.3 (2026-10-14, #83).
//devDependencies:@nimbus-sh/runtime: Nimbus numbers a runtime rebuild as a prerelease of its upstream version (3.13.14-1, the reproducible CPython core 0.16 requires), and semver ranks it below the plain 3.13.14, so a caret picks the older build. Both stay exact; move them with core.
//patchedDependencies: Every other dependency floats on a caret, newest by default. A patched one stays exact, since its patch applies to that version alone; each floats again with its patch removed, once upstream ships the fix the patch carries.
//patchedDependencies:agents: 0.29.0's MCP client chunk (as 0.26.0's) imports the MCP SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/client`, its cf-worker validator and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js`) statically, so every isolate's startup evaluated it, schemas and all, MCP or not: about 50 ms of `wrangler check startup`'s 470 at 7591e6fec. The patch loads it at the first MCP connection or RPC message (`loadMcpSdk`, before every manager path that creates a connection); a connection is made only once it has resolved. 0.29.0, the newest, still imports it statically. Its other hunks are the chat reconnect (`chat/react.js`, where 0.29.0's close now clears the protected answer and the patch restores it there instead), and `sql`'s query built once per template and the run-fiber recovery scan (`src-*.js`).
//patchedDependencies:workers-ai-provide: 4.0.1's binding chat model (as 4.0.0's) hangs on a body workerd holds open after `data: [DONE]`, misreads the shapes `Ai.run` returns when a concurrent call rewrote its shared options, drops binding refusals' status and Retry-After, asks no stream usage, emits no raw chunks, swallows unreadable events, ignores call headers (`x-session-affinity`), merges index-less native tool calls, finishes tool calls as `stop`, reports `usage.raw` as `{ total }`, reads no `workersAi` options, and streams a token twice when a chunk carries it in both `response` and `choices` (llama-3.3-70b). Delete once cloudflare/ai ships the fixes drafted in kinu-logs/agents-upstream/workers-ai-provider-binding-stream.md and workers-ai-provider-json-stream.md.
//patchedDependencies:@ai-sdk/provider-u: 5.0.65's `parseJsonEventStream` (as 5.0.53's) ignores `data: [DONE]`, so a producer that keeps the body open after it keeps the model stream open. Delete once vercel/ai ships the fix drafted in kinu-logs/agents-upstream/ai-sdk-sse-done-usage-only-chunk.md.
//patchedDependencies:@ai-sdk/openai-com: 3.0.75 (as 3.0.62) requires `choices` on every chunk, so Cloudflare's usage-only report without it (KINU-049) fails the step; and it converts the whole history again every step, which the patch converts once per frozen message (drafted in kinu-logs/main/AI-SDK-ASKS.md). Delete once vercel/ai ships the fix drafted in kinu-logs/agents-upstream/ai-sdk-sse-done-usage-only-chunk.md.
//patchedDependencies:@nimbus-sh/core: 0.27.0's session has no revision-checked write (NIMBUS-ASKS #55): the supervisor op writeFileIfRevision writes a whole file only over the revision its caller read (0: none), stat and write in one synchronous step, a file with no revision of its own refused ENOTSUP, and SessionRpc declares _rpcWriteFileIfRevision; worker and sdk carry the rest. And node-compat's createNodeFs extends node:fs's ReadStream and WriteStream when it is made, so it throws in the eval isolate (compatibility date 2025-06-01, where getBuiltinModule('node:fs') is undefined: armada 20261022090043-dc8e2d79); with none its streams are ENOSYS, as a face without descriptors already makes them; and its readFile with an encoding other than utf8 (base64, hex) answered the bytes decoded as UTF-8, where Node answers them in that encoding (#70). And setDefaultAcl let a confined principal set any default ACL on a directory it owns, so a share's viewer, refused `chmod o+w`, could make the same grant with `setfacl -d -m o::rwx` and open the project to the workspace's other agents: a confined principal's ACL may now only lose group and other bits of the one the directory holds, and what it creates grants others no write whatever its process umask (#74). Source and dist. Delete once Nimbus ships asks #55, #70 and #74 (/mnt/local/kinu/tmp/nimbus-asks/).
//patchedDependencies:@nimbus-sh/worker: 0.25.0 carries #55's _rpcWriteFileIfRevision (session/rpc.js, NimbusSession and the hosted session, all sending core's op). A program's tls.connect({ socket }) under an egress still fails with ERR_NIMBUS_EGRESS_STARTTLS, so STARTTLS (SMTP 587, pg ssl) cannot start; the staged shims (public/_assets/runtime/node-shims-df298aa46ab0bb20.js, its pinned sha256 re-stamped in dist/node-shims-artifact.generated.js) key every plain socket under an egress and ask the egress for TLS over a keyed one in-band, which Kinu's egress makes on the same server connection (#46: same-socket STARTTLS waits on workerd). Asks #42, #56 and #57's hunks are gone: shipped by 0.25 and 0.26. Delete with #55 and #46.
//patchedDependencies:@nimbus-sh/sdk: 0.21.0's files plane still writes with no precondition, so a hosted agent's checked save would read the file, compare it and write it in two calls, losing a write that landed between. files.writeIfRevision(path, content, expected) writes only over the revision its stat gave (0: no file), checked and written in one synchronous step at the session, through core's writeFileIfRevision supervisor op and worker's _rpcWriteFileIfRevision; a file with no revision (a mount's) is refused ENOTSUP. The remote endpoint does not carry it. Delete once Nimbus ships ask #55 (/mnt/local/kinu/tmp/nimbus-asks/).
